reasons: Overlaps on machine learning, deep learning, computational genomics
subject: scarce samples in genomics, from the other direction
body:
Hello Professor Kundaje,

My name is Vinil Polepalli and I am an undergraduate at New York University, pursuing a dual degree in Computer Science at the Courant Institute and Business at Stern. I am the sole author of a paper using conditional variational autoencoders to augment pan-cancer RNA-seq classification, which reached about 98% test accuracy across five tumor types on TCGA.

I read the Omni-ATAC paper, and what stayed with me is that the gain came from the protocol rather than the model: cutting background and mitochondrial reads lifted signal-to-background enough that archival frozen tissue became usable, which converts samples that were previously unreadable into training data. That scarcity is the problem I spent my own paper on, approached from the opposite side. I had 801 TCGA samples against 20,531 gene features, and instead of collecting more I trained a class-conditional VAE to generate synthetic expression profiles, which helped most on the underrepresented tumor types. What I would want to test is whether those two answers compose or interfere: given accessibility data recovered from archival samples too few to train on directly, does class-conditional generation add usable signal, or does it mostly smooth over the real variation the improved protocol was designed to recover.

In the past, I have worked on the following related projects:
- Sole author on cVAE-augmented deep learning for pan-cancer RNA-seq classification, about 98% test accuracy across 5 cancer types on TCGA: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.02743
- Hsp90 inhibitor virtual screening in the Chiosis Lab at Memorial Sloan Kettering: 4,566 candidates screened at 0.984 GNN ROC AUC and 5x enrichment, 0 Lipinski violations in the top 50: https://hsp90-dashboard.vercel.app/
- First author on a study of EGCG and piperine synergy in D. tigrina regeneration, using neoblast stem cells as a proliferation model (p < 0.05): https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06972

I have extensively used PyTorch, scikit-learn and Python in past work, along with standard genomics tooling, but have a lot of coding experience and am adaptable to whichever libraries your lab utilizes. Please let me know if there is a fit in your lab.

I would be happy to elaborate on my skills and where I think I can best help out.

Thank you!

--
Vinil Polepalli
New York University | Class of 2029
B.S. Computer Science (Courant) and B.S. Business (Stern)
vinil.polepalli@gmail.com
